# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. /usr/local/bin/playwright-cli
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is

interactive shell commands.

Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

HOW TO PLAY

THE STORY

Follow Carlos Santana through three chapters. Talk, choose what kind of player he becomes, train, then win the match to move on.

Progress saves automatically after every chapter.

ON THE PITCH

You always control Carlos, marked with a gold ring. Move, chase, pass, and shoot. Teammates and opponents play on their own.

  • WASDARROWS move
  • SPACE hold to charge, release to shoot
  • K pass · tackle when defending
  • L special moves menu
  • ESC pause

1v1 DUELS

When a defender steps up, the game freezes for a command duel. Pick DRIBBLE, PASS, SHOOT or SPECIAL, then stop the sweeping needle in the golden zone.

Timing adds up to +30 to Carlos's stat roll. Specials cost Samba energy.

SAMBA ENERGY

Dribble wins, passes, tackles and goals fill the bar. Spend it on:

  • SAMBA STEP20 — leave a defender behind
  • GOLDEN COMBI35 — one-two into space
  • SANTANA ROTATION55 — a spinning wonder shot

TOUCH & TABLET

Use the virtual stick and the SHOOT, PASS and SPECIAL buttons. Tap dialogue to continue. On a phone, landscape gives you the biggest pitch.

The game works in portrait too. Turn the phone for widescreen.

WANT TO WIN?

Shoot with the sweet spot: charge until the ring turns gold, aim with up/down, and release. Low shots into the corners beat most keepers.

A draw goes to golden goal, then penalties. The story waits for a win.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser game in the style of *Captain Tsubasa 2: Super Striker*, starring Carlos Santana, following his story from Salvador to the World Youth final.

## Requirements
- Game must be playable, story-driven, and visually polished, with original art/code/music.
- Support desktop and mobile/touch layouts, including portrait phones.
- No explicit framework; current repo is an empty PlayGround project.

## Decisions
- Built as a static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS canvas game (no build step), served from `index.html`.
- Three chapters: `SALT & SAND` (Salvador, 1994), `THE TRIAL` (São Paulo, 1995), `THE WORLD STAGE` (Tokyo, 1996).
- Gameplay hybrid: top-down 6v6 football + command/timing duels + special cutscenes, inspired by Super Striker.
- Specials: Samba Step (20), Golden Combi (35), Santana Rotation (55), filling a `SAMBA` tension bar.
- Procedural pixel art, portraits, WebAudio chiptune samba, localStorage save, keyboard + virtual joystick controls.
- Includes an in-game unofficial fan-tribute disclaimer.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`: full screen/menu/dialogue/duel/HUD/touch/penalty markup.
- `css/style.css`: complete responsive retro UI, desktop/portrait/landscape, CRT/scanlines, animations.
- `assets/fonts/`: bundled Press Start 2P and VT323 woff2 + OFL licenses.
- `assets/favicon.svg`.
- `js/story.js`: complete three-chapter story, choices, training configs, match configs, lineups, scripts, portraits metadata.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural music tracks, SFX, crowd ambience, mute persistence.
- `js/input.js`: keyboard, touch joystick, action buttons, input buffers.
- `js/pixel.js`: drawing helpers and procedural portraits for all characters.
- `js/scenes.js`: title/beach/street/locker/tunnel/stadium/home backgrounds with animated layers.
- `js/arena.js`: pitch/arena rendering, players, ball, match scene, training view.
- `js/cinematics.js`: Samba Step, Golden Combi, Santana Rotation, Drive Shot, save cinematics.
- `js/match-ui.js`: HUD, duel UI, special menu, pause, penalties, toasts/banners.

### Active
- `js/renderer.js` not yet written (orchestrates title/scene/match/training modes and screen shake/flash).
- `js/match.js` not yet written (core match simulation, AI, shooting/passing, goals, halftime, golden goal, penalties, scripts, specials).
- `js/main.js` not yet written (screen flow, story playback, training minigame, chapter progression, save/load, audio wiring, loop).
- No browser verification/screenshots yet; server not started.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/renderer.js` importing `drawTitleScene`/`drawScene` from `scenes.js`, `drawMatchScene`/`drawTrainingView` from `arena.js`, and `drawCinematic` through `arena.js`.
2. Create `js/match.js` implementing simulation, AI, duels, specials, scoring, halftime, golden goal, penalty shootout, and callbacks.
3. Create `js/main.js` tying screens, story beats, choices, training, match result, chapter/progress screens, credits, settings, localStorage, and requestAnimationFrame loop.
4. Start server on port 3002 and verify desktop + mobile with Playwright; fix runtime errors and visual issues.
5. Iterate on gameplay balance and screenshots; verify title, story, duel, special cinematic, goal, result, and portrait/mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM contract for all screens, IDs, buttons, canvas.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: all classes/IDs and responsive rules; contains `.screen`, `.stage`, `data-touch`, `data-screen` expectations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/story.js`: chapter data schema, match/lineup configs, `SAVE_KEY`, `CHARACTERS`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/arena.js`: exports `FIELD`, `GOAL`, `CENTER`, `drawPlayer`, `drawBall`, `drawMatchScene`, `drawTrainingView`; imports `drawScene`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/pixel.js`: exports `W=640`, `H=360`, helpers, `drawPortrait`, `CHAR_ART`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/scenes.js`: exports `drawScene`, `drawTitleScene`; cached bases.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/cinematics.js`: `drawCinematic`, called by `arena.js`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/match-ui.js`: `MatchUI` API used by `match.js`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: `AudioEngine` methods `init`, `unlock`, `playMusic`, `setCrowd`, `sfx`, `toggleMute`, `setMuted`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: `Input` API `take`, `isDown`, `vector`, `endFrame`, `isTouch`, `onFirstGesture`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: currently generic OMGithub README; optional game description update.

## Important Context
- Canvas is fixed logical 640×360; `FIELD={l:44,r:596,t:74,b:318}`, `GOAL={top:164,bottom:228,depth:13}`, center `(320,196)`.
- MatchUI expects Match properties: `score`, `clockLabel`, `halfLabel`, `tension`, `commentaryT`, `stats.shots`, `possessionPct()`, `config.venue`, `canShoot(player)`, `duel`, `getSpecialOptions()` (to be added), and callbacks for duel/special/pause/penalty.
- MatchUI callbacks expected: `onDuelCommand`, `onDuelLock`, `onSpecial`, `onSpecialClose`, `onPause`, `onSound`, `onResume`, `onRestart`, `onQuit`, `onPenalty`.
- Renderer must read `match.cine`, `match.charge`, `match.effects`, `match.flash`, `match.tension`, `match.state === 'goal'`, `match.lastGoalTeam`, `match.user`.
- Story flow: chapter pre beats → training → prematch → match → result → post beats → progress → next chapter; final chapter → credits.
- Choice effects are stat bonuses `{pace, technique, power, flair}`; chapter `baseStats` plus training bonus should feed match stats.
- `story.js` chapter 2 starts `specials: ['samba']`, scripts unlock `combi` at minute 15 and `rotation` at 31; chapter 3 has all three.
- Final chapter has script `{minute:66,type:'drive'}` for a scripted Tsubasa Drive Shot when Japan is not leading.
- Training configs specify `attempts`, `speed`, `zone`, `stat`, `scene`.
- Save key: `carlos-santana-camisa10-save-v1`; mute key `cs10-muted`.
- Working tree changes are uncommitted; no server running yet. Use `PORT=3002` (default server script supports `PORT`).
- Verify with Playwright; screenshots directory is gitignored (`screenshots/`).

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser game in the style of *Captain Tsubasa 2: Super Striker*, starring Carlos Santana, following his story from Salvador to the World Youth final.

## Requirements
- Game must be playable, story-driven, and visually polished, with original art/code/music.
- Support desktop and mobile/touch layouts, including portrait phones.
- No explicit framework; current repo is an empty PlayGround project.

## Decisions
- Built as a static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS canvas game (no build step), served from `index.html`.
- Three chapters: `SALT & SAND` (Salvador, 1994), `THE TRIAL` (São Paulo, 1995), `THE WORLD STAGE` (Tokyo, 1996).
- Gameplay hybrid: top-down 6v6 football + command/timing duels + special cutscenes, inspired by Super Striker.
- Specials: Samba Step (20), Golden Combi (35), Santana Rotation (55), filling a `SAMBA` tension bar.
- Procedural pixel art, portraits, WebAudio chiptune samba, localStorage save, keyboard + virtual joystick controls.
- Includes an in-game unofficial fan-tribute disclaimer.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`: full screen/menu/dialogue/duel/HUD/touch/penalty markup.
- `css/style.css`: complete responsive retro UI, desktop/portrait/landscape, CRT/scanlines, animations.
- `assets/fonts/`: bundled Press Start 2P and VT323 woff2 + OFL licenses.
- `assets/favicon.svg`.
- `js/story.js`: complete three-chapter story, choices, training configs, match configs, lineups, scripts, portraits metadata.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural music tracks, SFX, crowd ambience, mute persistence.
- `js/input.js`: keyboard, touch joystick, action buttons, input buffers.
- `js/pixel.js`: drawing helpers and procedural portraits for all characters.
- `js/scenes.js`: title/beach/street/locker/tunnel/stadium/home backgrounds with animated layers.
- `js/arena.js`: pitch/arena rendering, players, ball, match scene, training view.
- `js/cinematics.js`: Samba Step, Golden Combi, Santana Rotation, Drive Shot, save cinematics.
- `js/match-ui.js`: HUD, duel UI, special menu, pause, penalties, toasts/banners; `update()` commentary toggle patched so `say()` timers control visibility.
- `js/renderer.js`: orchestrates title/story/training/match/sheet drawing, screen shake, flash.
- `js/match.js`: complete 6v6 simulation, AI, passing/shooting, goals, halftime, golden goal, scripts, duels, specials, penalties, pause, reactions, result payload.
- `js/main.js`: title/menu, save/load, chapter select, story typewriter and choices, training minigame, prematch, match lifecycle, result/progress/credits, audio wiring, requestAnimationFrame loop.
- All JS files pass `node --check`.
- Static server running in tmux session `game` on port 3002; `curl` confirms HTTP 200.

### Active
- Browser verification with Playwright has started (`playwright-cli` located), but no page opened or screenshots captured yet.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002` with `playwright-cli` and capture desktop title screenshot.
2. Test full flow: New Story → dialogue/choice → training → prematch → kickoff; inspect console and network errors.
3. Exercise match controls: movement, charge shot, pass/tackle, special menu, duel timing, pause, goal, halftime, golden goal, penalties.
4. Verify result/progress/chapter transition/save/continue and credits.
5. Test mobile portrait and landscape layouts with touch controls and fix any overflow/visibility issues.
6. Iterate on gameplay balance, visuals, and any runtime errors found.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: screen flow, story playback, training, match lifecycle, save/load, audio and loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/match.js`: core simulation, AI, duels, specials, penalties, scripts, result object.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/match-ui.js`: HUD/duel/special/pause/penalty DOM controller; callback contract.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/story.js`: chapter schema, stats, lineups, scripts, save key, character data.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/arena.js`: pitch geometry, player/ball drawing, match/training views.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/renderer.js`: mode-based canvas rendering and shake/flash.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM IDs and screen/overlay markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: responsive layout, touch visibility via `body[data-screen="match"]`, overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/input.js`: keyboard/touch input API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: music/SFX/crowd/mute APIs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/pixel.js`: canvas constants, helpers, `drawPortrait`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/scenes.js`: `drawScene`, `drawTitleScene`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/cinematics.js`: special-move cinematics.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: still generic OMGithub README; optional game description update.

## Important Context
- Canvas is fixed logical 640×360; `FIELD={l:44,r:596,t:74,b:318}`, `GOAL={top:164,bottom:228,depth:13}`, center `(320,196)`.
- MatchUI callbacks implemented by `Match`: `onDuelCommand`, `onDuelLock`, `onSpecial`, `onSpecialClose`, `onPause`, `onSound`, `onResume`, `onRestart`, `onQuit`, `onPenalty`.
- `Match` exposes expected properties: `score`, `clockLabel`, `halfLabel`, `tension`, `stats.shots`, `possessionPct()`, `config.venue`, `canShoot()`, `duel`, `getSpecialOptions()`, `user`, `cine`, `charge`, `effects`, `flash`, `shake`, `state`, `lastGoalTeam`.
- Story flow: pre beats → training → prematch → match → result → post beats → progress → next chapter; final chapter → credits.
- Choice effects add to per-chapter `bonus`; training adds `trainingResult.bonus` to `trainingResult.stat`; `playerStats()` combines chapter `baseStats`.
- Save key: `carlos-santana-camisa10-save-v1`; mute key `cs10-muted`.
- Match result callback delivers after ~0.85s; `main.onMatchFinish()` destroys match UI and shows result.
- Testing server: `python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0` in tmux session `game`; use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`.
- Working tree changes are uncommitted; screenshots dir is gitignored (`screenshots/`).
- Potential verification focus: `Match.updateOver` invokes `onFinish` while still inside `Match.update`; main destroys UI during that call, so watch for post-destroy DOM errors.
